# ACEAPEX

> A lossless LZ77 codec that resolves every back-reference chain at encode time
> to its originating position and confines match search to the current block.
> Every block is therefore self-contained, so any 16 KB region decodes on a GPU
> without touching the rest of the file. Seven arXiv papers (2606.04268, 2606.18900, 2606.24531, 2607.18541, 2608.10188, 2609.16731, 2610.25149), MIT licensed, first row of lzbench 2.3.
> Every published claim is machine-checkable: a script emits one JSON record per
> claim and a fresh clone of the tagged release passes 17 of 17 CPU-reachable
> checks with none failing.

The class: random-access compressed VRAM layer. Not a ratio competitor — zstd-19
packs tighter on a whole-file window. Under an equal 16 KB independent-block
constraint, where every codec is equally seekable, ACEAPEX is first on three of
five corpora against zstd-19.

## Claims and evidence

- [Verified claims, machine-readable](https://github.com/yasha1971-coder/aceapex/blob/main/results.json): one JSON record per published claim — identifier, level R/M/E, expected value, tolerance, measured value, verdict, command.
- [Reproduction script](https://github.com/yasha1971-coder/aceapex/blob/main/reproduce_paper5.sh): `CHR1=/path/chr1.fa ./reproduce_paper5.sh` regenerates results.json on any host.
- [Repository guide](https://github.com/yasha1971-coder/aceapex/blob/main/REPOSITORY_GUIDE.md): what to read depending on why you came.

## Papers

- [Paper 1 — Parallel LZ77 decoding via encode-time absolute offset resolution](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.04268): the core design decision; CPU scaling; lzbench integration.
- [Paper 2 — Compressed-resident genomics](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18900): full device-resident GPU pipeline; 50 GB genome range-decode.
- [Paper 3 — Unified position-invariant random access through two compression layers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.24531): one coordinate seeks through both entropy and match layers; 0.334 ms, bit-perfect.
- [Paper 4 — What governs decode throughput in absolute-offset GPU LZ77](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18541): work granularity, not occupancy, governs throughput; encode-time min-match-length lever.
- [Paper 5 — What actually serializes GPU LZ77 decode](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10188): parse holds 64–72% of decode, not copy; chain depth moves latency by at most 2.8% and provably nothing where the file's own spike lives; self-overlapping matches are periodic fills, not chains, giving 2.75–8.42× on the match layer; the last sequential parse element is removed by the encoder for 0.540% of ratio.
- [Paper 6 — The price of random access: measuring block granularity across four compressed formats](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16731): nine axes across four formats; what 16 KiB independence costs and where a window-cost model holds.
- [Paper 7 — panvram: GPU-resident random access to a human pangenome cohort](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25149): 558 HPRC assemblies resident on one GPU as reference-relative archives; persistent-pool accounting and the cohort-scale locality effect. Code in a separate repository: https://github.com/yasha1971-coder/panvram

## Key measured numbers

- One 16 KB tile out of a 50 GB archive: 292–387 µs, independent of position; 1000 blocks (16 MB) in 0.423 ms.
- Region decode versus full decode on a genome: 845×. Silesia: 166×.
- Full device-resident decode on human chromosome 1: 71.0 GB/s, bit-perfect.
- Parse, not copy, holds 63.7–71.5% of decode time across four corpora.
- Bus efficiency 4.4%: a median match of 7 bytes against a 128-byte cache line; a coalesced write of the same data is 39× faster.

## What we refuted

- [Ten refuted hypotheses with numbers](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21874972), including one methodological error of our own — comparing a blockwise format against whole-stream zstd without equalising the constraint.

## Optional

- [Landing page](https://yasha1971-coder.github.io/aceapex/): class matrix, honest losses stated first.
- [lzbench 2.3](https://github.com/inikep/lzbench/releases/tag/v2.3): neutral third-party benchmark; aceapex 1.0.1 is the first row.

Note: ACEAPEX is an ongoing engineering investigation. Earlier papers and results document specific stages of the project and may be superseded. Current claims and their reproduction status are maintained in CLAIMS.md and results.json.
